page.overview:
Who is Guy?

While Guy's nationality was Japan in "Final Fight", in "Zero 3" it became the United States. As Guy's theme in "SFIV" is from "Zero 3", it was decided to use his nationality from the same game!

Guy was created by Akira Yasuda, who used Sho Kosugi as inspiration. Guy going to the United States of America after having failed the university admission exam mirrors Sho Kosugi who became distraught after failing twice and was convinced by his older sister to find fortune elsewhere, she then paid for her brothers flight to the United States.

Guy has many similarities to Ryu. Both are stoic, Japanese warriors trained by a great master, Zeku and Gouken. Both travel abroad to fight, and are friends/rivals with blonde American fighters, Cody Travers and Ken Masters, who are in relationships on their own (formerly in Cody's case). Both Guy and Ryu have inspired a young girl, Maki and Sakura respectively, and both share an enemy in M. Bison. Their interactions in the franchise may allude to their connections, either being impressed with each other's skill or being rivals.

Guy shares some similarities with [https://doubledragon.fandom.com/wiki/Jimmy_Lee Jimmy Lee] from another Arcade/Famicom brawler titled [https://doubledragon.fandom.com/wiki/Double_Dragon_Wiki Double Dragon] (1987) by Technōs Japan. Both are the secondary protagonist who wear red and brown clothing while also having brown hair and both accompany the main protagonist to help rescue the latter's kidnapped girlfriend (Guy helps Cody rescue Jessica Haggar while Jimmy helps his brother [https://doubledragon.fandom.com/wiki/Billy_Lee Billy Lee] rescue [https://doubledragon.fandom.com/wiki/Marian Marian Kelly]). The only difference is that each of them have their own separate love interests already. Jimmy fights against Billy in the hopes of winning Marian's love-- a kind of conflict that will never transpire between Guy and Cody.
